# Asian Games 2023 medal tally: Indian winners in Hangzhou - full list

India's Asian Games 2023 medal tally is 106 medals - 28 gold, 38 silver and 40 bronze. Know all Indian medal winners in Hangzhou and get medal table.

Picture by Hangzhou2022.cn

By Utathya Nag

A 655-member Indian contingent participated at the **Asian Games 2023** in Hangzhou, the People’s Republic of China from September 23 to October 8.

The 19th edition of the continental quadrennial multisport meet was originally scheduled for 2022 but was postponed by a year due to COVID-19.

India finished their Asian Games 2023 campaign with a record haul of 106 medals - 28 gold, 38 silver and 40 bronze.

This surpassed India’s previous record tally achieved at the last edition at Jakarta 2018, where a 570-strong Indian squad racked up 70 medals - 16 gold, 23 silver and 31 bronze.

China led the overall **Asian Games 2023 medals tally** with 201 gold, ahead of Japan (52) and the Republic of Korea (42).

Only four countries won over 100 medals in Hangzhou.

[Shooting](https://www.olympics.com/en/news/olympic-shooting-air-rifle-3-positions-rapid-fire-air-pistol-shotgun-trap-skeet) led the way for India at the Asian Games 2023 with an unprecedented haul of 22 medals, which included seven gold.

[Athletics](https://www.olympics.com/en/news/athletics-track-and-field-sprints-marathons-jumps-throws-heptathlon-decathlon), headlined by [Neeraj Chopra](https://www.olympics.com/en/news/neeraj-chopra-gold-medals-javelin-throw)’s successful title defence in the [javelin throw](https://olympics.com/en/news/javelin-throw-rules-regulations-and-all-you-need-to-know), came a close second with six gold along with 14 silver and nine bronze.

The [archery](https://olympics.com/en/news/archery-olympics-rules-disciplines-equipment-categories-bow-arrow) compound team, meanwhile, clean-swept the five gold medals in the category.

The [cricket](https://www.olympics.com/en/news/how-many-players-in-cricket) and [kabaddi](https://olympics.com/en/news/kabaddi-rules-regulations-how-to-play) teams also bagged two gold medals each while the men’s [hockey](https://www.olympics.com/en/news/field-hockey-rules-how-to-play) team’s gold secured a spot at the [Paris 2024 Olympics](https://www.olympics.com/en/news/paris-2024-olympics-india-medals-tally-winners-table).

India also earned their first [Asian Games](https://www.olympics.com/en/news/india-at-asian-games-history-medals) gold medal in [badminton](https://www.olympics.com/en/news/badminton-guide-how-to-play-rules-olympic-history) courtesy of the men’s doubles pair of Chirag Shetty and Satwiksairaj Rankireddy.

[Squash](https://www.olympics.com/en/news/squash-rules-how-to-play), [tennis](https://www.olympics.com/en/news/tennis-rules-regulations-how-to-play-basics) and equestrian completed the 28 gold medals for India in Hangzhou.

In addition to medals, Hangzhou offered 74 Paris 2024 Olympic quotas - six in archery, 10 in artistic swimming, 34 in boxing, two in breaking, two in hockey, 10 in modern pentathlon, six in sailing, two in tennis and two in water polo.

India secured six quotas in all – three in boxing ([Nikhat Zareen](https://olympics.com/en/news/who-is-nikhat-zareen-indian-boxer), Preeti Pawar, [Lovlina Borgohain](https://olympics.com/en/news/who-is-lovlina-borgohain-india-boxer)) and one each in athletics ([Kishore Jena](https://www.olympics.com/en/news/who-is-kishore-jena-india-javelin-thrower)) and men’s hockey.

The [2022 Asian Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Asian_Games "2022 Asian Games"), officially known as the **XIX Asian Games**, was the largest sporting event in [Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia "Asia") governed by [Olympic Council of Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Council_of_Asia "Olympic Council of Asia") (OCA). They were held from 23 September to 8 October 2023 in [Hangzhou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou "Hangzhou"), China, with 481 events in 40 sports and disciplines featured in the Games.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

In this edition of the Games, Brunei and Oman won their first ever medals when each country won a silver.[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-3) [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India_at_the_2022_Asian_Games "India at the 2022 Asian Games") became the fourth nation in the history of [Asian Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Games "Asian Games") after Japan, China and South Korea to cross the 100 medal-mark in one edition.[[4]](#cite_note-4)[[5]](#cite_note-5) The host nation, [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_at_the_2022_Asian_Games "China at the 2022 Asian Games"), crossed the 200 gold medal mark for the first time in a single edition of the Asian Games, reaching a total of 201 gold medals, becoming the first country in history to do so and surpassing their previous record of 199 golds in the [2010 Guangzhou Summer Asian Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Asian_Games "2010 Asian Games").[[6]](#cite_note-6)[[7]](#cite_note-7)[[8]](#cite_note-8) But on the other hand, China did not break the total medal record that was also held in Guangzhou with 416 medals in total. The mark of 41 NOCs winning medals is the highest for any Asian Games.

The **2022 [Asian Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Games "Asian Games")** (2022年亚洲运动会; *2022 nián yàzhōu yùndònghuì*), officially the **XIX Asian Games** (第十九届亚洲运动会; *Dì shíjiǔ jiè yàzhōu yùndònghuì*) and also known as **Hangzhou 2022** (杭州2022), were a continental [multi-sport event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-sport_event "Multi-sport event") which was held from 23 September to 8 October 2023 in [Hangzhou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou "Hangzhou"), China. The games marked the 110th anniversary since the creation of the first continental event, starting with the [1913 Far Eastern Championship Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1913_Far_Eastern_Championship_Games "1913 Far Eastern Championship Games").[[1]](#cite_note-2)

Originally scheduled to take place from 10 to 25 September 2022, on 6 May 2022 the Games were postponed to 2023 due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[2]](#cite_note-3) The new dates were announced on 19 July 2022, with the Games remaining branded as Hangzhou 2022.[[3]](#cite_note-4) Hangzhou was the third Chinese city to host the [Asian Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Games "Asian Games"), after [Beijing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing "Beijing") in [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_Asian_Games "1990 Asian Games") and [Guangzhou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou "Guangzhou") in [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Asian_Games "2010 Asian Games").

## Bidding process

The [Chinese Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Olympic_Committee "Chinese Olympic Committee") confirmed that Hangzhou in [Zhejiang province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang "Zhejiang") submitted a proposal to apply for the event and was the only city to complete all necessary steps to participate in the process who ended on end of August 2015. Hangzhou was officially awarded as the host city on 16 September 2015 in [Ashgabat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashgabat "Ashgabat"), [Turkmenistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkmenistan "Turkmenistan"), during the 34th [OCA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Council_of_Asia "Olympic Council of Asia") General Assembly.[[4]](#cite_note-5)

## Development and preparations

### Marketing

#### Emblem

The emblem of the Games, "Surging Tides" ([Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language"): 潮涌; [pinyin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinyin "Pinyin"): *Cháoyǒng*), was unveiled during a ceremony at the headquarters of the Hangzhou Culture Radio Television Group on 6 August 2018; it is designed to resemble a traditional [hand fan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hand_fan "Hand fan") from Zheijang, a [running track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_track "Running track"), the [Qiantang River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qiantang_River "Qiantang River") [tidal bore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tidal_bore "Tidal bore"), and radio waves (symbolising wireless connectivity). The organising committee stated that the emblem was meant to reflect "the great cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics gathering momentum in the new era", and "the unity, solidarity and development of the OCA."[[5]](#cite_note-6)[[6]](#cite_note-7)

#### Mascots

![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/48/%E6%9D%AD%E5%B7%9E%E7%AC%AC19%E5%B1%8A%E4%BA%9A%E8%BF%90%E4%BC%9A%E5%90%89%E7%A5%A5%E7%89%A9.jpg/250px-%E6%9D%AD%E5%B7%9E%E7%AC%AC19%E5%B1%8A%E4%BA%9A%E8%BF%90%E4%BC%9A%E5%90%89%E7%A5%A5%E7%89%A9.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)

The three mascots of the Games, Congcong (琮琮), Lianlian (莲莲) and Chenchen (宸宸), known collectively as the "Memories of Jiangnan" ([Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language"): 江南忆; [pinyin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinyin "Pinyin"): *Jiāngnán yì*, Jiangnan refers to roughly China's eastern regions south of the [Yangtze River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yangtze_River "Yangtze River")) whose name derives from the Tang Dynasty poet [Bai Juyi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bai_Juyi "Bai Juyi")'s famous sentence "When I recall Jiangnan, Hangzhou brings back most of my memories." ([Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language"): 江南忆，最忆是杭州; [pinyin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinyin "Pinyin"): *Jiāngnán yì, zuì yì shì hángzhōu*) were unveiled on 3 April 2020.[[7]](#cite_note-8) They are depicted as robotic superheroes originating from the [Archaeological Ruins of Liangzhu City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liangzhu_culture "Liangzhu culture"), the [West Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Lake "West Lake") and the [Grand Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Canal_(China) "Grand Canal (China)") respectively.[[8]](#cite_note-9)[[9]](#cite_note-10)

Congcong derives its name from the Cong jade pendant unearthed from the Archeological Ruins. Its body is coloured yellow, representing earth and bumper harvest and its head resembles mythical beast facial patterns. It is described as determined, sincere, kind-hearted, athletic and passionate.

Lianlian derives its name from the lotus leaves in the West Lake. Its body is coloured green, representing life and nature and its head resembles lotus leaf decorated with the Three Pools Mirroring the Moon, a scenic view of the West Lake, and the icon of Internet. It is described as pure, kind, lively, cute, elegant and hospitable.

Chenchen derives its name from the [Gongchen Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gongchen_Bridge "Gongchen Bridge"), a landmark structure in the Hangzhou section of the Grand Canal. Its body is coloured blue, representing science and technology and its head resembles [Qiantang River's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qiantang_River_Bridge "Qiantang River Bridge") tide with [Gongchen Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gongchen_Bridge "Gongchen Bridge"). It is described as brave, intelligent, optimistic and enterprising.

#### Motto

The official motto of the 2022 Asian Games, "Heart to Heart, @Future" was announced on 15 December 2019 to mark 1,000 days before the opening ceremonies. The motto is intended to symbolise the connectivity that the Asian Games create between the countries of Asia.[[10]](#cite_note-11)

#### Medals

On 15 June 2023, the 100-day countdown to the 19th Asian Games, the medal design named "Shan Shui" ([Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language"): 湖山; [pinyin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinyin "Pinyin"): *Húshān*) was released. Its design was inspired by Jade [Cong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cong_(vessel) "Cong (vessel)") in the Liangzhu Culture. The obverse featured the Games edition logo, misty hills, the city, a rippling lake and undulating mountains, while the reverse featured the Asian Games Sun Emblem and the name of the event in Chinese and English.[[11]](#cite_note-12)[[12]](#cite_note-13)

# Asian Games: All you need to know about Hangzhou 2022

![]()
![Copy Link](https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/content-reactions/check.png&h=80&w=80)

The Asian Games are here after a [year's delay](/espn/story/_/id/33864320/asian-games-2022-hangzhou-postponed-covid-pandemic). After an impressive Tokyo Olympics and equally creditable display at the Birmingham Commonwealth Games in 2022, India's top athletes prepare to make an impact at the continental level in Hangzhou, China.

Here's everything you need to know about India's campaign at the Asian Games (officially known as Hangzhou 2022).

## When are the Games starting?

Some sports - including football, cricket, sailing and hockey - have started a few days early but the official opening ceremony will be held on September 23 at the Hangzhou Olympic Sports Center Stadium. The Games end on October 8.

Indian interest at the Asiad began on September 19 with the [men's football team playing hosts China.](/football/story/_/id/38437026/asian-games-live-india-v-china-men-football-live-score-updates-commentary-hangzhou-sunil-chhetri-sandesh-jhingan)

***[Asian Games: Indian football teams return to Asiad, but preparations and results less than ideal](/football/story/_/id/38413946/asian-games-indian-football-teams-sunil-chhetri-asiad)***

## Editor's Picks

## [Asian Games: Who are India's top 10 gold medal contenders?](/espn/story/_/id/38446869/asian-games-india-top-10-gold-medal-contenders-hangzhou-2022-neeraj-chopra-satwik-chirag-hockey-team-archery-chess) Anish Anand

![](https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/photo/2023/0603/r1181994_1296x1296_1-1.jpg&w=130&h=130&scale=crop&location=center)

## [Asian Games: Indian hockey teams start favourites as they chase Olympic berths](/field-hockey/story/_/id/38448035/asian-games-indian-hockey-teams-favourites-chase-paris-olympic-berths-hangzhou-2022) Aaditya Narayan

## Which are the disciplines and sports at the Asian Games?

There will be 61 disciplines in 40 sports, including traditional Olympic sports and non-Olympic events. Medals will also be given in esports and breakdancing, which are making their debut.

Cricket is making a comeback this time after last featuring in the 2014 edition, and so is chess after 13 years.

Here are some of the [weird sports which will feature in this Asian Games.](/espn/story/_/id/38458410/hangzhou-asian-games-sports-never-heard-kurash-go-weiqi-sepaktakraw-dragon-boat-soft-tennis-wushu)

## What are India's prospects at the Asian Games?

India field a strong 655-member athlete squad, which includes some big names. Olympic gold medallist and world champion Neeraj Chopra will aim to defend his javelin gold medal against Pakistan's Arshad Nadeem. Boxing world champion Nikhat Zareen will look to win her first Asian Games medal while both men's and women's hockey teams will eye qualification to the Paris Olympics next year by winning gold medals.

However, Mirabai Chanu, Olympic and Asian Games medallist, will face tough competition from Chinese, North Korea and Thai weightlifters.

Here are [India's 10 best gold medal contenders](/espn/story/_/id/38446869/asian-games-india-top-10-gold-medal-contenders-hangzhou-2022-neeraj-chopra-satwik-chirag-hockey-team-archery-chess) at this edition's Asian Games (excluding cricket).

## What's the best way to plan the day to watch India's medals?

China is 2.5 hours ahead of India so the events will begin as early as 6 am IST and continue till around 8pm. In the first week (from September 24 to 30) shooting - where India can win multiple medals - qualification events start early in the morning, with the finals also ending before noon.

Preliminary rounds in archery also start early and the medal rounds are in the second week. Athletics medal events are scheduled in the second week and they will take place in the evening.

Here's our [detailed copy on the Asian Games schedule](/espn/story/_/id/38444437/asian-games-schedule-fixtures-medals-timings-hangzhou-2022), with a day-by-day breakdown.

## Who are the fresh faces from India to watch out for?

Aditi Swami (17), the reigning world champion in compound archery, is the one to watch out for. Like she did at the Worlds, Aditi could win medals for India in both women's individual and team events.

There is also exceptional young Indian chess talent at the Games, with D Gukesh and R Praggnanandhaa leading the men's squad. Jyothi Yarraji (hurdler) and Kishore Jena (javelin) can make an impact in track and field.

In wrestling, there's Aman Sehrawat, who's the Asian champion and Antim Panghal, a two-time U-20 world champion and now a World Championship medals.

Shooting has several young players too in a new-look squad as the sport looks to rebuild after the Tokyo Olympics blip. Teenagers Esha Singh, Shiva Narwal (10m air pistol) and Rudrankksh Patil (10m air rifle) are all gold medallists at the World Championships.

## Any top Indian athletes who are missing out?

Top wrestler and serial medal winner Vinesh Phogat will be missing out. So will Olympic silver medallist wrestler Ravi Dahiya and Rani Rampal, the Indian women's hockey team's superstar and former captain.

Read about the top names missing the Asian Games and the reasons for that here.

## What's India's Asian Games track record??

India have been decent performers at the Asiad, generally finishing among the top 10 countries and picking up more than 50 medals. Sports like athletics, shooting, boxing, wrestling have fetched multiple medals in each edition.

The country's best performance at the Asian Games happened in 2018 when the contingent won 70 medals -- 16 gold, 23 silver and 31 bronze.

However, India are nowhere near China and Japan in terms of overall medals at the Games. China have been constantly winning more than 100 gold medals at each Games since 1990 while Japan's overall tally generally touches 200 medals.

Fun fact: Last time the Asian Games took place in China -- Guangzhou in 2010 -- the host nation won 199 gold medals and in total 416 medals.

Safe to say, China will do everything to touch 200-mark this time.

## Where can I watch Asian Games in India?

Sony Sports Network will broadcast the Games on television while streaming will be live on Sony Liv website and app.

[浙江工业大学（屏峰校区）板球场

浙江工业大学（屏峰校区）板球场地为亚运会板球项目比赛场地，位于杭州西湖区、浙江工业大学屏峰校区内，西临图书馆，南侧为健行教学楼用房，北侧为上埠河，东侧为学校田径场，与校外城市主干道留和路相距约500米。场地含主比赛场和热身场，配备三层赛时配套用房，赛后可作为学校师生的活动中心。](#)

[杭州奥体中心体育馆

杭州奥体中心位于杭州市萧山区，杭州城市新中心，距离亚运村约3公里。场馆用地22.79公顷，总建筑面积39.695万平方米。地上主要包括体育馆、游泳馆、配套服务设施三大部分内容。建筑地下主要包括地下配套服务设施，机房及地下停车库。其中，体育馆为亚运会篮球项目比赛场馆，位于杭州奥体中心南端，总建筑面积74470平方米，约18000座，馆内能进行篮球、羽毛球、排球、乒乓球、手球、竞技体操、拳击、武术、室内足球等比赛。](#)

[黄龙体育中心游跳馆

黄龙体育中心游跳馆为亚运会水球项目比赛场馆，位于杭州市西湖区，风景秀丽的西子湖畔，处于整个黄龙体育中心的北部，在亚运村的西北方向且相距约11.5公里。总建筑面积48442平方米，观众席位数2938个。](#)

[中国杭州电竞中心

中国杭州电竞中心位于拱墅区，承担亚运会电子竞技比赛项目比赛。场馆似“星际涡旋”为设计理念，外形尤如“星际战舰”。](#)

[钱塘轮滑中心

钱塘轮滑中心为亚运会轮滑、滑板项目比赛场馆及训练场馆，位于杭州市钱塘新区杭州东部湾体育公园内。从高空俯瞰，场馆就像两个“6”融合叠加，也像一个“旋风陀螺”。](#)

[拱墅运河体育公园体育场
